name: Verlet rope & cloth
oneLiner: Capes, scarves, ribbons, hair tufts, banners, hanging ropes and chains that swing with movement and wind: a small Verlet solver (points and distance constraints, a strand or a 2D grid) pinned to an anchor on an actor or a post, with gravity, damping, gusts from game time, a ground line, solid rects and a body circle to drape over. Drawn as smooth shaded strips and quads with an ink outline, or whole pixels with a 1 px outline on pixel games. It only reads anchors and only draws: hit boxes and rules never change. Fixed 1/120 s sub-steps, so ?t=&freeze=1 is deterministic; a teleporting anchor re-poses its cloth hanging at rest instead of stretching it across the screen.
fits: side-scrolling platformer / action (capes, scarves, banners, hanging ropes)
top-down action RPG (capes, ribbons, banners in town)
metroidvania and soulslike-lite heroes with a cape or scarf
turn-based or tactics battles (banners, capes on idle units)
any 2D game drawn on a canvas, pixel or HD
notFor: 3D or WebGL-rendered characters (this is a 2D canvas solver and drawing)
gameplay ropes (grappling hooks, swinging on ropes, rope bridges you walk on): the cloth never affects the player; use a physics rule for that
cloth that must collide with every sprite in the scene (only a ground line, a short rect list and one body circle per piece)
very large cloth (sails, curtains covering the screen): fine up to a few hundred points per piece, not thousands

needs: a fixed update step that calls update(dt) once per step after movement (also run by ?t= fast-forward and ?auto=1)
for each attached piece an anchor: world position (shoulders, neck, head, pole top, beam) and facing of the actor or post, or null while hidden
the draw pass of each actor (draw the actor's pieces right before / after its sprite) and of the scenery
optional: camera offset when the game subtracts it by hand; a ground line or solid rects; swing / dash / hit events for impulses
provides: cloth and rope pieces drawn behind or in front of their actor (capes and hair behind, scarves in front, banners and ropes in the scenery)
automatic teleport handling (snap) on respawn, restart, room change and blinks
wind(x, y): the same wind for grass, smoke or particles
tip(id): the free end of a rope or chain, to hang a lantern or bell on
stats() and list(): points, snaps, stretch, reach, pin error, resets (for tests)

params.label: View (auto: top-down when anchors return fx, fy)

assets: module/verlet-cloth.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_Cloth): Verlet strands and grids, anchors with teleport snap, wind from game time, ground / rects / body collision, painted HD drawing (smooth silhouette, fold lighting from a light direction, back face, length gradient, brush texture, lit rim, thin hue edge, trim, twisted rope strands; `look: 'flat'` keeps the v1.1 flat tones) and a whole-pixel rasteriser with a 1 px outline; skins only give the ink, outline width, pixel mode and default colour
no image or audio files of its own (the demo's hero and backdrop come from the shared demo-kit; posts, poles and fittings are painted in code)

module.skin: optional: skins/skin-api.js + a skin, passed as `skin` (ink, outline width, pixel mode, default colour)
